newsitem.title: UK: Copper 1997 TC/RCs rise 11 percent - Brook Hunt.
newsitem.headline: Copper 1997 TC/RCs rise 11 percent - Brook Hunt.

text.p: Benchmark treatment costs/refining charges (TC/RC) for 1997 have been established at $105 a tonne (T/C) and 10.5 cts/lb (R/C), up 11 percent from 1996, industry analysts Brook Hunt and Associates said.

"With world concentrate output forecast to rise by only two percent in 1997 and global smelting capacity by 4.2 percent, concentrate stocks are expected to fall this year," Brook Hunt said in a special report.
But the impact of declining ore inventories will not be felt by custom smelters until the middle of the year.
"This is because most of the surplus concentrate accumulated during 1995 and 1996 is already sitting in the storage yards of custom smelters, as opposed to being held by miners," it said.
However, a large part of this surplus will be depleted by the end of the year, and spot TC/RCs will fall sharply during the second half. Metal prices are also expected to fall during this period.
Looking ahead, Brook Hunt said that an additional 880,000 tonnes of mine capacity and an extra 350,000 tonnes of extra smelter capacity is firmly committed and due onstream in the period to 2005.
"Hence, for a period of several years post 1998, falling copper metal prices are expected to be the key factor in determining future treatment and refining charges," it added.
